• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
Drive can read the user's files, but it may refuse to move or trash a file that wasn't made through this connector, even one the user owns. Before you move a file with update_file, check the file's canMoveItemWithinDrive capability; before you trash a file with trash_file, check its canTrash capability. If the results you have don't show them, call get_file_metadata for that file first. Skip each file where the value is false, because Drive will refuse the change, and do the rest. If Drive refuses a file anyway, don't retry it, request access, or make a copy; carry on with the other files. At the end, tell the person which files you skipped or Drive refused, with a link to each, and that they can make those changes in Drive.
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

# PR B, part 2: the agonist's design for (IV) the deferred-search flag and (V) the reduced render page

Agonist report, 2026-11-27, for DR-2026-08-19 §7 (agonist-antagonist; a blind antagonist attacks this next).
Branch head `ee815a82`, schema `user_version` 167. **Design only; nothing is implemented.** Read-only on the
repository and on `data/guidebook.db`, whose sha256 was `3d419efb…edb9` before and after every probe
(`sha256sum data/guidebook.db`). Dry runs used scratch copies only: my own at
`/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/f8d4d6c2-8f72-53c6-8e31-d3258750c5f6/scratchpad/p2/s.db`, and, read-only,
the path-finder's `…/scratchpad/pf/r3MOB.db`, which holds the live 3 × MOB determination the engine wrote
(specification 9) on the same canonical base.

Rule 7a: every figure below was read today, and its command sits beside it. Re-run the command rather than
trust the figure.

---

## 0. Answer in brief

- **(IV) Add one flag, `amend-search --set-deferred-reason TEXT`, and the converse refusal on
  `--set-absence-class`. No migration.** `deferred_reason` already exists, is nullable `TEXT` with no CHECK,
  and the write path already carries an UPDATE of it (dry run, §1.3). Re-running the four searches does not
  fix the defect on its own: the four old rows would still read as searches that ran and found nothing,
  because every reader classes a zero-result row as empty when `deferred_reason` is NULL. That is OD-45's
  ACTION (4), and five readers follow it today. Re-running is owed in addition (OD-45 ACTION (3)), as
  research.
- **(IV) A second defect, found in the dry run:** `amend-search --set-absence-class` today writes a row that
  is both deferred and classed. On a scratch copy, exec 9 took `genuine_absence` beside its
  `deferred_reason`, rc 0. That is the state `log-search` refuses as "A row cannot assert both".
- **(V) A new static-HTML script, `scripts/generate/determination_page.py`.** Its core is a pure function,
  `page(conn, specification_id) -> str`, and the CLI writes the result outside the repository (refused
  inside it, including the committed `scratchpad/`), for publication as a private Artifact.
  `owner_browser_build.py` is a whole-database table browser (sql.js with the database embedded), so it
  cannot be the renderer. A page that embeds every row can refuse nothing. Only its out-of-repo guard and its
  stamp are reused.
- **(V) The page refuses four things:** a determination that is not live; any non-English cell it would
  print that lacks a current, reviewed, hash-matching English rendering; a printed source with no
  verification standing (NULL); a governing source with no population-match row for the cell's identity
  lens. It does **not** refuse an UNVERIFIED source. The owner ruled "keeping them but they get a triangle
  warning", and C10 (after T-117 4a) is the one gate for that.
- **(V) It must show every population-match row, never `assess_cell.population_match`'s first.** On the 3 ×
  MOB cell, six governing sources carry contested grades (PARTIAL and PROXY), and that function returns
  PARTIAL for each, which hides the dissent.
- **Two variants of the four OD-63 figures.** Which one is built depends on the owner's Q1. Variant B
  depends transitively on **T-124, T-059 and T-068** (T-124's own preconditions), plus the unit cleanup data
  (T-108, T-086, T-111) and T-113. It needs **no T-036 view and no migration**. It must refuse while any
  code-stratum figure of the cell is unparsed: 28 of 51 such rows on 3 × MOB today.

---

## 1. (IV) The deferred-search flag

### 1.1 The wrong thing that reaches the guidebook today (proved)

DR-2026-08-19 §4 publishes the determination's "search log *including the empty searches*". Four
zero-result rows on parameter 3's slug never ran:

```
$ python3 - <<'PY'   (canonical, read-only)
... select exec_id, slug, engine, results_found, absence_class, deferred_reason, substr(findings_note,1,200)
    from search_executions where results_found=0 order by exec_id
(87,  'accessible-circulation-geometry', 'googlebooks', 0, None, None, 'NOT A ZERO-YIELD — AN UNFIRED QUERY, AND I RECORDED IT AS A NULL THREE TIMES BEFORE A CHECK CAUGHT IT. All three requests returned HTTP 429: …')
(133, 'accessible-circulation-geometry', 'web', 0, None, None, "RETRIEVAL FAILURE, NOT ABSENCE: curl exit 35 (connection reset by peer) …")
(138, 'accessible-circulation-geometry', 'web', 0, None, None, 'RETRIEVAL FAILURE, NOT ABSENCE: HTTP 403 (919-byte interstitial) …')
(191, 'accessible-circulation-geometry', 'web', 0, None, None, 'RETRIEVAL FAILURE, NOT ABSENCE: … HTTP 202 with a 180-byte HTML stub …')
```
Totals: `select count(*), sum(absence_class is null), sum(deferred_reason is not null), sum(results_found=0) from search_executions` gives `(203, 203, 1, 13)`.

**The reader a page would use already publishes them as empty.** `db.cell_status` (T-034) is the one home
of "which searches belong to a parameter". Run on a scratch copy:
```
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=$S/s.db python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import db;r=db.cell_status(3)['stages']['research'];print([e for e in (87,133,138,191) if e in r['examined_empty']])"
in examined_empty: [87, 133, 138, 191]
```
`examined_empty` is documented as "looked at and found nothing" (`grep -n 'examined_empty' scripts/db.py`,
the docstring of `cell_status`). Five more readers treat `results_found = 0 AND deferred_reason IS NULL` as
an empty search, and all of them count these four:
- `research_batch_dod.py` R8 and R14;
- `alias_provenance_audit.py:136`;
- `test_scan_contract.py:1492`;
- `v_coverage_parameter_via_admission`;
- every `v_coverage_*` view through `deferred_reason IS NULL`.

**No typed home exists.**
```
$ GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=$S/s.db python3 scripts/db.py amend-search --exec-id 87 --append-note "TASK-FIXTURE probe" --set-deferred-reason "HTTP 429" --session session_p2-probe --dry-run
db.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --set-deferred-reason HTTP 429     rc=2
$ ... amend-search --help | grep set-absence-class
  --set-absence-class {genuine_absence,query_shape_failure,wrong_index}
```
The page could separate these rows only by parsing the `findings_note` prefix ("RETRIEVAL FAILURE, NOT
ABSENCE"). That is a fact read out of prose, which CLAUDE.md §4's schema-shape rule forbids ("a prefix that
says what the rest of the cell means").

**Second defect (the converse).** On a scratch copy:
```
$ GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=$S/s.db python3 scripts/db.py amend-search --exec-id 9 --append-note "TASK-FIXTURE probe: classing a deferred row" --set-absence-class genuine_absence --session session_p2-probe
{ "exec_id": 9, "appended": true, ..., "absence_class": "genuine_absence" }   rc=0
row after: (9, 0, 'genuine_absence', 1)     # results_found, absence_class, deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
```
`log-search` refuses this exact state (`scripts/db.py`, `log_search`: "--deferred-reason says the search was
not run, and --absence-class … says it ran and found nothing. A row cannot assert both"). No CHECK or
trigger holds it: the table CHECKs name `absence_class` only against `results_found`, and
`select name from sqlite_master where type='trigger' and sql like '%search_executions%'` prints `[]`.
Whichever flag lands second must refuse a row that already carries the other.

### 1.2 The ruling text applied

- **OD-45**, delegated, check confirmed (`references/project-standards.md:6391`–`6404`). *"A logged search
  whose request returned no result list (a 403 or bot challenge, a 429, a connection reset, a stub page) is a
  search not run: recorded with `deferred_reason` naming the failure, with no absence class, and owed a
  re-run."* ACTION: *"(1) Log a request with no result list as deferred, with its reason. (2) Give it no
  absence class. (3) Re-run it. (4) Read a zero-result search as a finding only where `deferred_reason` is
  NULL."*
- **DR-2026-08-19** line 1039: *"`deferred_reason` is for searches *not run*, never a findings channel."*
  Lines 373–375: the acceptance criterion quoted above.
- **CLAUDE.md rule 8**: *"Vocabularies come from the schema, not a list in code"*. `deferred_reason` has
  **no CHECK** (schema above: `deferred_reason TEXT, -- non-NULL => deliberate no-search for this cell`), so
  it holds no vocabulary to read. It is free text naming the failure, exactly as `log-search
  --deferred-reason` takes it. Adding a vocabulary would mean inventing terms (rule 8: "never invents a
  vocabulary term") and writing a migration nothing needs. `absence_class` keeps its three values: OD-45
  (option (c)) adds none, and T-081 §3 says so.

### 1.3 The smallest change

**Files:** `scripts/db.py` only (one function, its argparse, its dispatch), plus the test, the skill prose
and the stale comment (§1.6).

*Before* (`scripts/db.py`, `amend_search`; locate by symbol): the SELECT reads `… results_found,
absence_class` and has no `deferred_reason`. The `set_absence_class` block checks `results_found` and
write-once, not deferral.

*After*, in outline:
```python
def amend_search(..., set_absence_class: str = None, set_deferred_reason: str = None):
    row = conn.execute("SELECT …, results_found, absence_class, deferred_reason FROM search_executions …")
    any_setter = (... or set_absence_class or set_deferred_reason is not None)
    ...
    if set_absence_class:
        ...existing refusals...
        if row["deferred_reason"] or (set_deferred_reason or "").strip():
            raise Refusal(f"exec {exec_id}: deferred_reason says this search was not run; an absence class "
                          f"says it ran and found nothing. A row cannot assert both (OD-45). Nothing was written.")
    deferral_set = None
    if set_deferred_reason is not None:
        reason = set_deferred_reason.strip()
        if not reason:
            raise Refusal(f"exec {exec_id}: a blank --set-deferred-reason states no cause. Nothing was written.")
        if row["results_found"] != 0:
            raise Refusal(f"exec {exec_id}: results_found={row['results_found']}. A search that returned a result "
                          f"list ran; deferred_reason means NOT run, never a findings channel (R6). Nothing was written.")
        if row["absence_class"]:
            raise Refusal(f"exec {exec_id}: absence_class is {row['absence_class']!r}: the row says it ran. A row cannot "
                          f"assert both (OD-45). Nothing was written.")
        if row["deferred_reason"]:
            raise Refusal(f"exec {exec_id}: deferred_reason is already set. It is write-once. Nothing was written.")
        conn.execute("UPDATE search_executions SET deferred_reason=? WHERE exec_id=?", [reason, exec_id])
        trail = f"{marker}deferred_reason set (OD-45: the request returned no result list; a search not run, owed a re-run)"
        conn.execute("UPDATE search_executions SET findings_note=? WHERE exec_id=?", [(merged or "").rstrip() + trail, exec_id])
        merged = (merged or "").rstrip() + trail
        deferral_set = reason
    ... return {..., "absence_class": absence_set, "deferred_reason": deferral_set}
```
Argparse, beside `--set-absence-class`:
```python
p_am.add_argument("--set-deferred-reason",
    help="OD-45: a search logged as run whose request returned no result list (blocked, rate-limited, reset, "
         "a stub page) was NOT run. Records why in deferred_reason (free text; the column has no CHECK). "
         "Write-once; refused when the search found anything or carries an absence class.")
```
Dispatch: pass `set_deferred_reason=args.set_deferred_reason`.

- **What each part reads:** the same row SELECT as today, plus `deferred_reason`. No vocabulary is read,
  because none exists.
- **Rollback is already sound.** A refusal raised after the note append rolls back. Measured on a scratch
  copy: a refused `--set-absence-class` on exec 1 (results 20) left its note length at 88 before and 88 after.
- **Dry run of the write path, scratch only.** I set `deferred_reason` on exec 87 by hand on
  `p2/s.db` and ran `python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py --scratch $S/s.db --out /dev/stdout`. It
  printed `UPDATE "search_executions" SET "deferred_reason" = '…' … WHERE "exec_id" = 87;` and `0
  insert(s), 1 update(s), 0 delete(s)`.
- **After that write:** `cell_status(3)` moves 87 out of `examined_empty` and into
  `never_examined.deferred_searches == [87]`, and `v_deferred_acts` lists `('search', 'exec 87
  accessible-circulation-geometry')`.
- **Size estimate** (an estimate, not a count): about 25 lines in `db.py` and about 45 lines of tests.

**Re-running is not an alternative.** A re-run is a new row (R8, append-only), and the old row stays as it
is. `v_deferred_acts`' header says so: "A search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges"
(`select sql from sqlite_master where name='v_deferred_acts'`). Without the flag, the four old rows keep
publishing as empty searches whether or not they are re-run. The flag is the fix; the re-run is the debt
OD-45 ACTION (3) records, and it is research (log-search rows, with the Internet Archive route, CLAUDE.md §7).

### 1.4 The red test first

File `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py` (registered, advisory, battery `tests`: `grep -n -A8 'id:
test_run_pipeline_refusals' governance/check-registry.yaml`). New section `T081A` placed after `T080`.
Prefix check: `git grep -c -E 'T081A' -- scripts/tests` prints nothing today.

**Fixture.**
- Inside the file's own `scratch()` copy, the subject row is chosen by query: `SELECT exec_id FROM
  search_executions WHERE results_found=0 AND deferred_reason IS NULL AND absence_class IS NULL ORDER BY
  exec_id LIMIT 1`.
- If that returns nothing, build the row by HAND on a second copy, marked TASK-FIXTURE. This follows the
  file's R3-10 rule, because `log-search` can no longer write such a row (T-080).
- A deferred row is chosen by `deferred_reason IS NOT NULL`, a found row by `results_found > 0`, and a
  classed row by building one with `log_search(..., absence_class=…, dry_run=False)` on the copy.
- A feature probe (`'set_deferred_reason' in inspect.signature(db.amend_search).parameters`) makes each case
  go **red by name** on today's tree instead of crashing.

| Case | Assertion | Red today because |
|---|---|---|
| `T081A-01` | `amend_search(eid, note, set_deferred_reason="TASK-FIXTURE HTTP 429")` succeeds. The row's `deferred_reason` is set and `absence_class` stays NULL. The row leaves `cell_status(P)["stages"]["research"]["examined_empty"]` and joins `never_examined.deferred_searches`. It appears in `v_deferred_acts`. | no such parameter (probe red); the CLI exits 2 on an unrecognized argument |
| `T081A-02` | Each of these is refused with "Nothing was written" and leaves the row unchanged: a blank reason; a row with `results_found > 0` (names R6); a row with `absence_class` set ("cannot assert both"); a row already deferred ("write-once"); both flags in one call. | flag absent |
| `T081A-03` | `--set-absence-class` on a deferred row is refused ("cannot assert both"), and `absence_class` stays NULL. | **red on a real defect:** today it succeeds (exec 9, rc 0, §1.1) |
| `T081A-04` | Through the CLI, `amend-search --help` lists `--set-deferred-reason`, and a refused call prints the `REFUSING` prefix. | flag absent |

**After-test:** all four pass. The `T080` cases still pass. `test_db_amend_writers.py` (its `v_deferred_acts`
counts are derived: `git grep -n 'deferred_reason IS NOT NULL' scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py`),
`research_batch_dod.py --selftest` and `test_scan_contract.py` give the same before/after failure lines.

### 1.5 Migration needs (rule 3)

**None for the tooling.**
- The column exists, nullable `TEXT` with no CHECK: read `PRAGMA table_info(search_executions)` and the
  table's DDL.
- It is writable, because `amend-search` already writes `search_executions`, so `dbcore.writable_tables`
  covers it.
- The write path captures the UPDATE (dry run above).

The **data** (deferring 87, 133, 138 and 191, each with its reason in the note's words) is T-081's research
PR (R1), landed through `emit_data_migration.py` after this merges (rule 10). Prove that PR with
`migration_reproducibility.py --deep`: the row-count check cannot see an UPDATE (rule 3).

### 1.6 Callers to sweep (rule 4)

- **Code:** `scripts/db.py`, three places (argparse `p_am`, the `elif args.command == "amend-search"`
  dispatch, the `amend_search` signature). Also the stale comment in `log_search` (`grep -n "amend-search\`
  writes only" scripts/db.py`: "amend-search writes only findings_note and harm_finding"), false already and
  made more false by this change. Correct that one line.
- **Readers whose behaviour changes as intended**, re-run before and after with nothing edited:
  - `v_deferred_acts`;
  - the `v_coverage_*` views and `v_coverage_parameter_via_admission`: the four rows' pairs return to owed,
    which is correct, because nothing ran;
  - `db.cell_status`;
  - `research_batch_dod.py` R6, R8 and R14 (R8's empties count falls by the rows deferred; R6 stays clean
    because the flag refuses `results_found > 0`);
  - `alias_provenance_audit.py`;
  - `test_scan_contract.py` T026-14 (its expected `EXAMINED` is derived from the same predicate, so it moves
    with the data).
- **Skills (prose callers):**
  - `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:135`–`137`: add "or, for a row already written as run whose request
    returned no result list, `amend-search --exec-id N --append-note … --set-deferred-reason '<the failure>'`".
  - `skills/research-log-manager_SKILL.md` step 3: one sentence for the same case.
- **Workplan:** `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-081-classify-zero-result-searches.md`
  §4 item 1 (third bullet), §6 and §8 say "`amend-search` has no deferred-reason flag … the row is not
  amended here". Once this merges, that is false, and T-081's research procedure must say to defer the four
  through the flag. Edit it in this PR, or in PR A's hygiene follow-up.
- **Graph:** `python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py --check` before and after, because a
  refusal's text is added. Report the difference only.
- **Mention only:** `architecture/meta-scripts-spec.md:59`. `governance/research-contract.yaml` R6 stays true.

### 1.7 What reads the addition (§8)

T-081's research batch writes it for the four rows. `cell_status`, `v_deferred_acts` and the coverage views
read the column, and the render page (V) reads it to print "not run, owed a re-run". **Without it**, four
retrieval failures publish as evidence that nothing exists on the ramp slug.

### 1.8 What I would delete

Nothing in code. In the workplan, T-081's "list it in the pull request as a deferral" workaround.

### 1.9 Stop conditions

- `deferred_reason` gains a CHECK or a trigger before this lands (re-read the schema).
- The dry-run UPDATE is not captured by `emit_batch_sql.py`.
- Any reader in §1.6 holds a typed count that goes red, rather than a derived one.
- The owner reverses OD-45 (its reversal condition: "the owner wants a blocked request kept as a finding
  about a source's reachability").

### 1.10 Open owner inputs

None required. OD-45 is delegated and confirmed. The owner may reverse it, which would turn this flag into
the wrong home.

### Defects (worst first)

**D1 — HIGH. The page mixes two databases.** Design §2.4: `page(conn, specification_id)` is "a pure function over a read-only connection", yet reads `db.translations_shown()` and `db.cell_status()`, neither of which takes a connection: both open `dbcore.connect(readonly=True)`, which resolves `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` or the canonical file (`dbcore.py` `def db_path` and `def connect`, `target = Path(path) if path is not None else db_path()`). With `--db scratch.db` and no matching env var, the value and grades come from the scratch copy and the translations and search log from canonical. T037R-05 ("a --db other than the canonical file prints DRAFT") is the exact case where this bites, and no case would see it. Correct fact: the two helpers bind to `db_path()`, not to a passed connection (`grep -n "def translations_shown\|def cell_status" scripts/db.py`).

**D2 — HIGH. The DRAFT test cannot fire under the project's own write path.** "--db is not dbcore.db_path()'s canonical file": `db_path()` returns `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` when set, and CLAUDE.md §4 requires that variable inline on every call to a scratch copy. A page built that way reads as canonical and prints no DRAFT. `dbcore.is_canonical` exists (`dbcore.py` l.119; `grep -n "def is_canonical" scripts/dbcore.py`) and is what the comparison has to be against.

**D3 — HIGH. A ratified ruling on the page's form was not found.** Owner rulings 2026-10-30 ACTION (3) "do not restore a static generator"; ACTION (7) makes the "committed HTML" narrowing unratified; ACTION (4) requires both lenses; items 5 and 7 fix the comparison table's rows and scope. None is cited in design §2.2. The design proposes to edit the skill sentence that restates ACTION (3) ("reconcile"), i.e. to change prose that carries a ruling instead of asking the owner. Command: `sed -n 4852,4867p references/project-standards.md`.

The correct closure on HEAD ee815a82: Variant A = T-117 {T-120, T-068 {T-059 {T-120, T-127 {T-102}}}, T-102} + (IV) + T-110 data; Variant B = Variant A + T-124 + T-108, T-086, T-111, T-113 data (+ an in-scope filter, T-036 or equivalent). The "A is the short path" framing that Q1 is put to the owner on is therefore materially overstated.

**D5 — MEDIUM. The contested grades are a correction, and the determination used the withdrawn one.** See claim 6. The page as designed prints both rows "as a contest" (which CLAUDE.md §4 permits) but says nothing about which one the engine used, so a reader sees PARTIAL and PROXY with no sign that the published value was graded on PARTIAL.

**D6 — MEDIUM. Apparatus prose reaches the published page through `claimed_unit`.** The design bans `value_note`, `falsification_condition`, `confidence_*`, `tier_basis`, `derivation_rationale` (T037R-03) and prints `claimed_unit` "as stored". On spec 9, extraction 80's unit reads "… Digit-equivalents are an editorial gloss, not verbatim -- see notes and GAP filed this batch on _require_verbatim's digit-check." and its value is `viisi prosenttia` (Finnish words, no English owed by `_translations_owed`). Variant A prints both.

**D7 — MEDIUM. §1.6's predicted reader effect is false on the target slug.** "The four rows' pairs return to owed": measured, pairs_searched, jurisdictions and languages are unchanged (other searches cover KR/KO, SG/EN, NL/NL), only `searches_outside_scope` drops 68 → 67. A test written to that prediction would be red for the wrong reason.

**D8 — MEDIUM. Refusal 4 re-implements `population_match`'s attribution and is undefined for an ICF- or need-only cell** (claim 5d). It contradicts the design's own §2.11 stop condition.

**D9 — LOW. The setter's refusals omit admissions.** `results_found = 0` does not imply no `search_admissions` edge (no CHECK pairs them); a row with an edge ran.

**D10 — LOW. NULL-verification refusal examines nothing today and treats NULL more strictly than the engine does** (claim 5c).

**D11 — LOW. Variant B's colour code depends on 28 unparsed governing code-stratum figures that the engine nonetheless governed on** (spec 9 links them as `governing`). Whether the engine's value is right with 28 figures `figure_refusal` cannot read is outside this design, but Variant A publishes that value. [UNVERIFIED: how the engine treated those rows.]

### Omissions (callers and facts the design missed)

- `db.get_coverage_completeness` (`coverage --slug`, cited in `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md` §4): output changes (`searches_outside_scope`, `searches_deferred_with_reason`).
- `governance/research-contract.yaml` R6: "deferred_reason means DELIBERATELY NOT SEARCHED". A 429 is not deliberate; OD-45's plan changes asked for a sentence on "deliberate". That text is injected every session by the SessionStart hook in `.claude/settings.json` and compared by the blocking `research_contract_sync`, so any edit touches a blocking check. The design says "R6 stays true".
- The DDL comment `deferred_reason TEXT -- non-NULL => deliberate no-search for this cell` (needs a schema migration to change; at minimum a PR sentence, as OD-45 asked).
- `amend_search`'s docstring ("APPEND a correction to a logged search's findings_note. Never rewrite it.") and the `p_am` help string ("APPEND a dated correction …"): already inaccurate, made more so.
- `skills/citation-miner_SKILL.md` l.120 and `scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py` R6 message repeat "DELIBERATELY NOT SEARCHED".
- T-037 §3's own evidence ("no page generator", `ls scripts/generate`) is already false (owner_browser_build.py exists since 2026-10-28), so T-037 as written stops at its §3; the design does not say so.
- `v_deferred_acts` keeps every deferred search listed after its re-run ("Not derivable today"); deferring four rows adds four permanent entries. The design reports the listing as the intended effect and omits the permanence.
- Readers the design lists by line number (`test_scan_contract.py:1492`, `alias_provenance_audit.py:136`) are fine; tests that derive their counts from the same predicate (`test_run_pipeline_refusals.py` l.1232, 1262, 1276; `test_db_amend_writers.py` l.4303, 4391) move with the data and belong in the before/after run.

def amend_search(exec_id: int, note: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False,
                 set_harm_finding: bool = False,
                 set_target_evidence_type: str = None,
                 set_origin: str = None, set_mined_ref_id: str = None,
                 set_origin_pass_id: int = None, add_result_artefacts=None,
                 clear_target: bool = False, set_absence_class: str = None):
    """APPEND a correction to a logged search's findings_note. Never rewrite it.

    --clear-target (2026-09-27, exec 77 / DR-2026-09-26 5.2d). --set-origin's own
    refusal below requires target_tier/target_evidence_type/target_scope to be NULL
    before an origin can move off 'planned' -- correctly, per OQ-7 (R1: no) -- but
    until now nothing could NULL them: --set-target-evidence-type only ever swaps one
    declared value for another. That left a ratified correction unexecutable through
    the CLI, which CLAUDE.md names as a coverage bug to fix, not a licence to hand-write
    SQL. Clears all three together, because the refusal tests them as a group ("a
    lookup targets no tier") and a partial clear would leave the row in the same
    refused state. Combinable with --set-origin in one call: the refusal below reads
    the EFFECTIVE post-clear values, not the stale pre-call row, so
    `--clear-target --set-origin incidental` in one call is how a lookup is corrected --
    there is no ordering in which two separate calls would both succeed.

    R8 makes search_executions an append-only log: a query is logged verbatim before
    screening and empties are kept, so no writer may edit what a search recorded at
    the time. But a note can be WRONG, and leaving a wrong one standing is worse than
    the rule it protects. On 2026-09-02 exec 34 recorded that the Euan's Guide Access
    Survey is "predominantly information provision, toilets and staff attitude rather
    than circulation geometry" — a characterisation written from a 404 page, and false
    on the actual report, whose most-cited barrier is "could not get around the venue
    (lack of lifts, narrow corridors, too little space or poor layout)" at 56%. That
    sentence was the whole reason the batch's one disability-led source was not
    admitted, and until now nothing in the CLI could correct it.

    So: append, with a dated marker, in the '|| CORRECTED <date>:' form the record
    already uses. The original text is never touched, which is what R8 protects, and
    the next reader sees both what was believed and what was established.
    """
    note = (note or "").strip()
    if not note:
        raise Refusal(f"exec {exec_id}: refusing to append an empty amendment.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT exec_id, findings_note, harm_finding, "
                           "target_evidence_type, mining_direction, origin, "
                           "mined_ref_id, origin_pass_id, query_text, "
                           "target_tier, target_scope, results_found, absence_class "
                           "FROM search_executions WHERE exec_id=?", [exec_id]).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(f"exec {exec_id}: no such search execution.")
        stamp = audit(session)
        marker = f" || CORRECTED {stamp['created_at'][:10]}: "
        any_setter = (set_harm_finding or set_target_evidence_type or set_origin
                     or set_mined_ref_id or set_origin_pass_id is not None
                     or add_result_artefacts or clear_target or set_absence_class)
        duplicate = note in (row["findings_note"] or "")
        if duplicate and not any_setter:
            return {"exec_id": exec_id, "appended": False,
                    "reason": "this amendment is already on the row"}
        merged = row["findings_note"] or ""
        if not duplicate:
            merged = merged.rstrip() + marker + note
            conn.execute("UPDATE search_executions SET findings_note=? WHERE exec_id=?",
                         [merged, exec_id])

        # Effective target_* values AFTER this call, used by --set-origin's refusal
        # below instead of the stale pre-call `row` -- so --clear-target and
        # --set-origin combine in one call rather than deadlocking across two.
        eff_target_tier = row["target_tier"]
        eff_target_evidence_type = row["target_evidence_type"]
        eff_target_scope = row["target_scope"]
        cleared = None
        if clear_target:
            if set_target_evidence_type:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"exec {exec_id}: --clear-target and --set-target-evidence-type "
                    f"together -- clear removes the value, set retypes it. Pick one.")
            was = (row["target_tier"], row["target_evidence_type"], row["target_scope"])
            if was == (None, None, None):
                raise Refusal(

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The refusals the run-pipeline skill states and no writer held (2026-11-06).

WHY THIS EXISTS (CLAUDE.md section 8). Two independent operator walk-throughs of
`skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md` on scratch copies of the database wrote, through the
sanctioned CLI, every row the skill says is refused: a `verified` extraction over an
abstract-scope reading (OR-11a), an extraction on an UNVERIFIED source with no reading
recorded, a fabricated claim text behind a false `--verbatim-exempt`, a numerical row with
no locator, a `full` reading of a publisher landing page, a parameter direction with the
rationale "no admitted source read", a term minted beside its near-duplicate, a NAMES-NEW
adjudication to an existing term, a harm finding with no `insufficient` edge, a connection
at SPECULATIVE confidence with a hand-typed id and a retired target, a search with an
unknown slug, language or merged parameter, a hand-typed ref_id, a conflict between a
population and itself, and Crossref's own affiliation-as-author deposit written as six
corporate co-authors. What reaches the guidebook without these cases: a page that prints
"verified" over a figure nobody read in full, a value attributed to a source that was
never obtained, a direction nobody can trace to a document, and a byline that lists a
university five times.

Round 2 (same day) adds the cases for the second pass over the same walk-throughs: what is
owed has one home (R2-1), a real search is never refused for its pairing (R2-2), a block
reason is an obstacle the ledger classes (R2-3; a reading no longer clears it, R3-1), a
damaged byline behind a malformed deposit is still a cross (R2-4), `full` is checked
against what the scan can count (R2-5; the deposit inference was removed, R3-3), the
exemption is refused where a body is held, for observe-term too (R2-6), a slug must exist
(R2-7), a reference id is computed (R2-9), a connection type has an arity row (R2-10), a
flag that says "live vocabulary" prints it (R2-11), a comparator word is refused in a NAME
only (R2-12), the verified-scan reader examines every live extraction (R2-15) and the
skill-vocabulary audit can go red (R2-16).

Round 3 (same day) lands the third review's repairs, each with the real shape the reviewers found as
well as a synthetic one: a block and a reading are two facts and the ledger (migration 124) says which
holds (R3-1); a decodable body includes a PDF with a text layer and the exemption needs a persisted page
render (R3-2); `full` over a page-less text lands as the operator's claim, marked `uncounted` (R3-3); the
id of a promotion is derived from the document's identity (R3-4); a repeated author is one author (R3-7);
the ledger's header names every block reason (R3-8); the vocabulary audit takes files and cannot pass on
nothing (R3-9); a flag's vocabulary is read from its column (R3-12); a conflict names the flag it refuses
and never takes the scope marker (R3-14); a `.md` session and a foreign `--stamp` do not reach a row
(R3-15, R3-16); `coverage` reports the slug's status (R3-17).

TEST-DESIGN RULE (R3-10). A fixture selector never raises. When the live corpus no longer offers the state
a case needs (every source VERIFIED, scan debt at zero, every parameter given a direction), the selector
builds it by hand on the scratch copy (marked HAND) or the case prints SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE with the reason:
counted apart from EXAMINED, never silent. A case that depends on a round-2 or round-3 feature is gated by
a probe (`hasattr`, a `sqlite_master` read, a `--help` read, a result key) and goes red BY NAME when the
feature is absent, so an older tree fails case by case and does not crash. The writer's judgement about
which block reasons restate a typed fact has one home, `db._BLOCK_REASON_COPIES`, and is read, not restated.

Nothing here types a count, an id or a code the database can derive; a state the CLI cannot build is made
by SQL on a second copy and marked HAND. A legitimate change to the data (a first real connection, a scope
fill, a new identity code, a source becoming VERIFIED, a parameter given a direction) moves a derived
number, never a relation asserted. Each case shows the refusal fires AND the legitimate shape still passes.

Runs on a COPY of the canonical database (dbcore refuses the canonical file read-write) against a scratch
retrieval-log root of symlinks to the tracked sessions plus the fixtures written here; each scratch copy
of the database gets its own root, because a source minted on a copy takes an id the main copy will mint
too. What an audit's own `--selftest` asserts (research_batch_dod's BLOCKED fixtures) is not repeated.

CREATE VIEW v_deferred_acts AS
-- v_deferred_acts: every deferral that still STANDS, one row each, with the date it was first recorded.
--   kind                subject
--   search              the exec id, with its slug when it has one
--   mining              the mined ref_id and the slug
--   reading             the ref_id and the parameter (or the whole source)
--   adjudication        the observation id, its ref_id and its surface form
-- ref_id and parameter_id are the same facts as columns, so a writer asks "is this pair already deferred?" of this
-- view and cannot disagree with it (db.py defer-reading does). They are NULL where the kind has none. For a reading
-- they are the EFFECTIVE pair (see below), which is the pair the ledger owes.
-- deferred_at is the date the obligation was FIRST recorded (created_at), never the date a row was last written: a
-- re-deferral that reset the clock would hide an old obligation. An older search row carries only a date; every other
-- row, and any search logged now, a minute.
--
-- WHAT STANDS, per kind (a standing deferral is one nothing has since discharged):
--   search        EVERY deferred search. A search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges, so a
--                 deferred search whose cell a later search covered still lists. Not derivable today.
--   mining        every citation_mining row whose OWN deferred_reason is set. The source's citation_mining_status is
--                 not read: it is one fla

1. **For each row the command prints, read its whole `findings_note` and its `query_text`, and decide its cause under R14 and OD-45 as resolved under delegation (section 2).** Write it with `db.py amend-search --exec-id N --set-absence-class <value> --append-note "<one sentence: which words of the note decide it>" --session "$STEM"`. The verb refuses a value outside the column's CHECK and a row already classed.
   - A note that names the cause in R14's own words decides it (for example a note that calls the zero "GENUINE WELL-FORMED" with the anchor resolved, or "ZERO FROM THIS INDEX, NOT ABSENCE" because another index holds citations).

Exec id 81 calls itself "an R14 query-shape failure of a kind R14 does not name": judge it on its own words, not as one of these.
2. **A row whose note does not let you decide** is not classed: list it in the pull request with the note's words and leave it. Do not guess a cause.
